title: Shared compression library: debug run reached, validation blocked
subtitle: codex (gpt-6) · line: xswap-compression-tiering · base 5e84ca92 · 1 candidate · 2 guests / 1 build

verdict.headline: The debug guest completed, but parser defects blocked validated coverage.

sections.title: Same candidate, further debug evidence
sections.lead: R2 continues the original shared-library hypothesis on unchanged kernel source. A corrected debug setup reached the guest; the complete correctness matrix still gates every performance measurement.

blocks.text: The fresh baseline guest passed. The candidate debug build enabled KASAN and its guest completed. The saved integration result remains failed because strict parsing rejected an expected diagnostic.
R2 consumed 2 guests and 1 build. With the original contract, C1 has spent 5 guests and 4 builds. No calibration or performance comparison ran.

sections.title: 1. Whole system: restore the application page
sections.lead: An application needs its full page in physical RAM. Stored contents may be compressed inside RAM or reside on a backing device. Compression trades CPU work for less storage traffic.

blocks.takeaway: The changed engine serves compressed contents inside RAM
blocks.note: Schematic path, with no illustrative size or timing used as a measurement.

blocks.text: The candidate changes the compressed-storage implementation. The existing frontend still decides admission, accounting and writeback. No new RAM-to-disk migration policy is implemented here.

sections.title: 2. Subsystem: policy keeps the object identity
sections.lead: ZSwap retains the entry index, memory-group charge, ordering and lifetime pins. A shared page library owns per-CPU codec contexts, scratch buffers and compressed-object storage.

blocks.takeaway: Data moves through the engine; policy stays with the frontend

blocks.text: High-confidence source review supports this ownership boundary. Each successful store returns a caller-owned handle; publication, charging and release stay with ZSwap. The retained debug log adds observations, while the full matrix remains incomplete.

sections.title: 3. Concrete change: the same kernel reached the debug guest
sections.lead: The candidate source is unchanged. R2 repaired the debug configuration, advancing from a build gate to recorded guest output; evidence parsing then stopped formal coverage.

blocks.takeaway: R2: guest output reached a rejecting parser

blocks.text: The retained log reports PASS for 6 subcases and ok for 3 named KUnit cases, with no kernel warning found. These are raw observations; the original integration result remains failed.

The parser rejected the deliberate invalid-codec message. Diagnostic replay also exposed a false rejection of the standard skip:0 summary. Corrected replay diagnoses those rules; it creates no new successful guest observation.

sections.title: Repair parsing, then collect fresh counted evidence
sections.lead: Keep the failed result and archive intact. A separately frozen correction must validate fresh correctness evidence on the same source before calibration or dependent architecture phases.

blocks.takeaway: Required validation still separates observations from a result

blocks.text: Confidence is high in the two observed parser defects. A kernel diagnostic, failed raw subcase or unexplained replay mismatch would stop continuation. Remaining resources and the earlier enforced deadline stay binding.
